### Changed
- **Protenix-v2 normal mode is about 2 % faster on Blackhole.** Triangle multiplication writes its gated output and
  moves the pair stream in bfp8 where a fused tail reads it, as Wormhole normal already does. Paired cold folds read
  1.7 s faster at a median of 79 s; accuracy unchanged on 44 paired folds of the 11-complex test set (same-seed
  structure 0.07 A apart against a 0.60 A bar, docking success 35/44 on both). `--fast` and Wormhole are unchanged.
- **RFdiffusion3 is about 2.5 % faster on Wormhole.** The diffusion transformer computes q, k and v in one projection
  and normalises and splits them into heads in one kernel. Page design 35.98 -> 35.09 s in `--fast`; designs are
  byte-identical. Blackhole is unchanged.

## Highlights

- Genes with NaN counts are ignored with a warning instead of raising an error, and get NaN dispersions, LFCs and p-values (#502).
- `plot_MA` and `plot_dispersions` take matplotlib axes through a new `ax` argument (#504).
- A fitted `DeseqDataSet` can be written to h5ad (#477, #510).
- An empty count matrix raises a clear error (#503).
- LFC shrinkage and the dispersion fitting fallbacks were corrected (#470, #471, #472), as were `poscounts` size factors for genes whose positive counts are all 1 (#494).
- The synthetic example dataset ships with the wheel, so `load_example_data` works without the repository (#467).
- The documentation has a new tutorial on continuous covariates (#507).
- PyDESeq2 works with pandas 3.1 and anndata 0.13 (#456, #501).
- The test suite compares PyDESeq2 with DESeq2 1.50.2, which it runs through rpy2 (#505).

## Changed behaviour

- Status updates and timings are logged through the shared scverse logger and are hidden by default (#506).
  Set `scverse_misc.logging.config.verbosity = "info"` to see them.
  `summary()` and `lfc_shrink()` still print their results table.
- `uns["trend_coeffs"]` and `uns["vst_trend_coeffs"]` are dicts with the keys `a0` and `a1` instead of pandas Series, and `obsm["design_matrix"]` is a plain DataFrame (#477, #510).

_releases.body:
- **bugfix**: serialization now fails fast when a covariance function (or a predictor) belongs to a class that could not be resolved again on loading. Mellon stores classes by name and recovers them with `getattr(import_module(module_name), classname)`, so a class that is not bound at the top level of its module — most commonly one defined inside a factory function — produced a file that `Covariance.from_dict` / `Predictor.from_json` could not load. Previously `to_json()` wrote that file without complaint and the `AttributeError` surfaced only at load time, potentially long after the fit it was meant to preserve. `to_json()` / `to_dict()` now raise a `TypeError` naming the offending qualified name and asking for a module-level definition. Module-level covariance functions, including user-defined ones, are unaffected and still round-trip exactly; existing serialized files still load. `Predictor.copy()` is deliberately not affected, as it never resolves the predictor class by name.
 - the guard above lives in `Covariance.__getstate__`, which is also Python's `copy`/`pickle` hook, so `copy.deepcopy()` and `pickle.dumps()` of such a covariance function now raise the same `TypeError`. Previously `deepcopy` succeeded, since it carries the class by reference instead of resolving it by name; `pickle` failed on its own. Only classes that were already unserializable are affected. For the same reason `Predictor.copy()` of a predictor with such a covariance function now raises `TypeError` up front instead of the previous `AttributeError` from the load path — it did not work before either.
 - composite covariance functions (`+`, `*`, `**`) now record the full module of their class instead of only the top-level package, so a user-defined `CovariancePair` subclass living in a subpackage can be resolved on loading. Files written by earlier versions continue to load unchanged.
 - `compute_d_factal` is renamed to **`compute_d_fractal`**, correcting the spelling of "fractal". The new name is the canonical one and is what `d_method="fractal"` now calls internally. **`compute_d_factal` continues to work**: it is retained as an alias that forwards to `compute_d_fractal`, is still exported from `mellon.parameters`, and remains listed in `__all__`, so existing code needs no change. **No deprecation warning is emitted** — the old name is used widely enough downstream that a warning on by default would be noise rather than signal. Callers writing new code should prefer `compute_d_fractal`.
 - **removed**: the `mellon-test` console script. It was declared as `mellon-test = "pytest:main"` while `pytest` is only a `dev` extra, so on a normal install it failed immediately with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pytest'`. It could not have worked even with `pytest` present: the installed distribution contains only the `mellon` package, never the test suite, and the script invoked `pytest.main()` with no arguments — so it would have collected from whatever directory it happened to be run in. Run the tests from a source checkout with `pytest` instead. **This removes a published command**, so any script invoking `mellon-test` will now get "command not found" rather than the `ModuleNotFoundError` it got before.
 - **bugfix**: declare `packaging` as a runtime dependency. `mellon.base_predictor` has imported `packaging.version` at module scope since v1.5.0, but `packaging` was never listed in the project dependencies, so installing Mellon into an environment that provided only its declared requirements failed at `import mellon` with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'packaging'`. Environments that happened to supply `packaging` transitively — including any install of the `dev` or `docs` extras — were unaffected, which is why it went unnoticed. If you have ever hit `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'packaging'` on a fresh install of Mellon, this is the fix.
 - the GP leverage diagonal `diag(B M^-1 B^T)` is now computed with a Cholesky solve instead of an explicit `jnp.linalg.inv(M)`. `M = sigma^2 K_uu + B^T B` (plus jitter) is symmetric positive definite by construction, so the inverse was never needed. All five sites are converted: `_LandmarksConditional._compute_obs_variance` and `._leverage` (scalar and per-feature sigma) and `_LandmarksConditionalCholesky._leverage`. Results are unchanged to within rounding (worst relative difference 1.8e-7 across 30 public-API comparisons; 1.9e-4 on a real 5,000-landmark problem with cond(M) = 2.5e13, where both forms agree with a QR reference to about 1e-4 and neither is uniformly the more accurate).
 - this also removes a segfault. `jnp.linalg.inv` lowers to LU (`getrf`), which dispatches to OpenBLAS's threaded `dgetrf_parallel`; at 5,000 landmarks that routine overflows the stack of the thread JAX calls it on and the process dies with SIGSEGV. Measured on OpenBLAS 0.3.30: 12/12 crashes end-to-end at `OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=16` against 0/12 at 1 thread, and 6/12 against 0/12 for the unpatched and patched code run back to back (not concurrently). Affects any caller using landmarks with `obs_variance=True` or `Predictor.leverage()`. The Cholesky path uses `potrf` and is unaffected. `export OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1` remains a valid workaround on older versions.
 - note: with `jitter=0`, or in float32, the Cholesky form returns NaN for matrices where the old `inv` returned finite values. In every such case checked the old values were numerically meaningless (errors above 25%, leverages outside [0, 1]), so this surfaces a failure that was previously silent. The default `jitter=1e-6` in float64 — what every estimator uses — is unaffected.

_releases.body:
### Fixed

- `pt.aliphatic_index()` no longer returns a diluted number for an ambiguous residue, and `pt.molar_extinction_coefficient()` no longer assumes an unspecified residue is not a chromophore. Both counted a residue they could not place as zero while still counting it in the length, so `pt.aliphatic_index("AJILAVIL")` gave 256.25 where `AVILAVIL` gives 292.5, although `J` is leucine or isoleucine and both occupy the same aliphatic volume. An ambiguous residue is now resolved when every amino acid it stands for contributes the same amount (`J` is 3.9 for the aliphatic index, and `B`, `J` and `Z` are exact zeros for both numbers, since none of aspartate, asparagine, leucine, isoleucine, glutamate or glutamine is aliphatic or absorbs at 280 nm), and refused with `PeptacularError` when they differ. `X` stands for any amino acid, so it is always refused: its aliphatic volume is unknown, and it could be tryptophan or tyrosine. A residue outside the twenty (`U`, `O`) is a determinate zero for both, because it is a defined residue that is neither aliphatic nor a chromophore. `pt.instability_index()` is unchanged and still refuses every residue with no `DIWV` entry, which is every one of these, because no ambiguity code can be resolved there: the two amino acids a code stands for have different `DIWV` values. So the aliphatic index of a peptide holding `J` is determined while its instability index is not, and the two now say so. The published benchmark values are unchanged.

- A charge carrier error in a comma-separated list now carries the position of the carrier that is wrong. `pt.parse("EMEVEESPEK/[Na:z+1,H:z+1^0]")` reported `Position 12`, the first carrier, while the bad multiplier is in the second at `Position 19`, which is where a malformed carrier in the same list already pointed. The message also no longer writes `Invalid charge carrier` twice when the carrier parser names the carrier itself: `/[Na:Z+1]` read `Invalid charge carrier 'Na:Z+1': Invalid charge carrier 'Na:Z+1': a charge carrier must be a bare charged formula`.

- **`pt.parse` is stricter about charge carriers.** `parse` now checks the syntax of each charge carrier between `/[` and `]` with the same function that resolves it for `mass()` and `mz()`, instead of copying any text through. A string whose carrier is impossible as written used to parse and serialize, then raised `ProFormaFormatError` the first time `charge_state` or `mz()` was used; now `pt.parse` raises that error up front, naming the carrier and its position. This covers `EMEVEESPEK/[]`, `EMEVEESPEK/[garbage]` and `EMEVEESPEK/[Na:zX]`, and also a carrier whose formula cannot be read, such as `/[M+2H]` or `/[+2Na+]`. Code that parsed such a string and never asked for a mass or m/z will now get an exception. `pt.validate` returns `False` for them as before. Valid carriers (`/2`, `/-1`, `/[Na:z+1]`, `/[Na:z+1,H:z+1]`, `/[H-2Na1:z+1]`, `/[Na:z+1^2]`) parse and give the same charge states and m/z as before, and modification names (`PEP[Foo]TIDE`) are still resolved lazily. The Pyteomics and psm-utils adapters report a target library's unreadable charge text as a failed round trip, as they did before.

- `pt.fragment()`, `pt.fast_fragment()`, `pt.fragment_arrays()` and `ProFormaAnnotation.frag()` raise `UnsupportedOperationError` for a cross-linked or branched peptidoform instead of returning the ions of the linear peptide. A `#XL` or `#BRANCH` label on two residues bonds those residues to each other, so a single backbone cleavage between them does not separate the two halves and the ions at those positions do not exist: `pt.fragment("EVTK[X:DSS#XL1]LEK[#XL1]SEFD", ion_types=("b",), charges=(1,))` returned b4, b5 and b6 at 596.329, 709.413 and 838.456 as if K4 and K7 were unlinked. That bond is not modelled (ProForma 2.1 section 9.2, see `PROFORMA_COMPLIANCE.md`), and the interchain form (`//`) is already refused when parsed, so the intrachain form is now refused too and `pt.diagnose(seq, "fragment")` reports it. `mass()`, `neutral_mass()`, `mz()` and `comp()` are unchanged and still describe the intact molecule. A label on one residue only is a dead-end linker, which bonds nothing and still fragments as an ordinary modification, and a localization group such as `#g1` is not affected.
- `count_residues` and `percent_residues` count the residues inside an interval instead of counting the interval as one residue. With an interval anywhere in the sequence the counts did not sum to the sequence length: `pt.count_residues("PEP(?TI)DE")` returned a `(?TI)` key and a total of 6 for a 7-residue peptide, and `(?PEP)TIDE` totalled 5 for 7 residues, so `percent_residues` was computed over the wrong total. Now `T` and `I` are counted individually. An interval without modifications adds no key of its own. An interval with modifications is written onto each residue it spans as a one-residue interval with the same modifications, so `PEP(?TI)[Phospho]DE` holds `(?T)[Phospho]` and `(?I)[Phospho]`, which keeps the modification visible and apart from a localised `T[Phospho]`. `include_mods=False` and `split` are unchanged.
- `count_residues` and `percent_residues` write interval keys that `pt.parse` reads back when the interval meets a terminal modification or a global isotope label. The residue's whole key was wrapped in the interval's parentheses, so `[Acetyl]-(?PEP)[Phospho]TIDE` gave `(?[Acetyl]-P)[Phospho]`, `PEPTID(?E)[Phospho]-[Amidated]` gave `(?E-[Amidated])[Phospho]` and `<13C>PEP(?TI)[Phospho]DE` gave `(?<13C>T)[Phospho]`, and all three raise `ProFormaFormatError` when parsed. The parentheses now hold the residue and its own modifications only, giving `[Acetyl]-(?P)[Phospho]`, `(?E)[Phospho]-[Amidated]` and `<13C>(?T)[Phospho]`. The counts are unchanged (#113).
- `pt.count_residues()` and `pt.percent_residues()` no longer carry the parent's annotations into their keys. Counting a charged peptide used to give `{'P/2': 2, 'E/2': 2, …}` instead of `{'P': 2, 'E': 2, …}`. A labile modification gave `{+79.966}P`, an unlocalised one `[Phospho]?P`, and a name `(>Name)P`. The keys now hold the residue and the modifications localised to it, including its own N- or C-terminal modification, so `pt.count_residues("PEPTIDE/2") == pt.count_residues("PEPTIDE")`. A global isotope label stays in the key, because it applies to every residue, so `pt.count_residues("<13C>PEPTIDE")` gives `{'<13C>P': 2, …}` (#105).
- `pt.split()` no longer refuses a peptide whose localization group spans more than one residue. The guard that stops a slice cutting a group fired on the per-residue slices a split makes, so `pt.split`, `pt.count_residues`, `pt.percent_residues`, `pt.permutations`, `pt.combinations`, `pt.combinations_with_replacement`, `pt.product` and `pt.sort` all raised `PeptacularError` on valid ProForma such as `PEPT[Phospho#g1]IDEK[#g1]`. A split keeps every position, so every member of the group is still present across the pieces and `pt.join(pt.split(seq))` returns the original, scores included. A partial slice, a digest or a coverage comparison that would cut a group still raises.
- Slicing or digesting an annotation whose localization group (a primary tag plus `#label` references) would be split between the slice and the rest now raises `PeptacularError` naming the group, instead of silently dropping the modification or leaving a dangling `#label` reference. A group wholly inside the slice is unchanged.
- `averagine_comp` no longer rounds each element on its own. It keeps the integer compositions within 1 Da of the requested monoisotopic mass and returns the one whose isotope envelope best matches the fractional averagine envelope. Independent rounding put `pt.averagine_comp(1000.0)` at 978.5134 Da, 21.49 Da short; it now lands within 0.5 Da. Element counts stay non-negative integers within 2 of `estimate_averagine_comp`.
- ProForma JSON non-finite-number errors consistently include the rejected value (`nan`, `inf`, or `-inf`) when encoding objects, decoding mappings, or parsing JSON constants.
- `pt.iter_batch()` and every function that takes `n_workers` or `chunksize` name the rejected value in the message instead of only the parameter. `pt.iter_batch("mass", sequences, errors="bogus")` said `errors must be 'raise' or 'collect'` and now says `errors must be 'raise' or 'collect', got 'bogus'`; `batch_size=0` says `batch_size must be a positive integer, got 0`. The validator is shared with the parallel helpers, so `pt.mass(sequences, n_workers=0)` reads `n_workers must be a positive integer, got 0` (#81).
- ProForma JSON type errors name the type they received. `pt.from_proforma_dict` on a document whose `sequence` is a number said `sequence must have type str | None` and now says `sequence must have type str | None, got int`. The same holds for the object checks (`names and modifications must be JSON objects, got names int and modifications dict`), the array check (`modifications.internal must be an array or null, got int`) and the modification-count check (`N-terminal modifications must map modification strings to integer counts, got str -> str`) (#80).
- `pt.fragment()`, `pt.fast_fragment()`, `pt.fragment_arrays()` and `ProFormaAnnotation.frag()` return the internal and satellite ions of a peptide whose localization group spans more than one residue, instead of raising `PeptacularError`. The guard that refuses a slice cutting a localization group fired on the per-ion slices the fragment engine makes, so `pt.fragment("PEPT[Phospho#g1]IDEK[#g1]", ion_types=("i",), charges=(1,))` raised `Localization group #g1 would be cut by slice [3:4]` where 5.1.0 gave 8 immonium ions. It affected the immonium, by, ay, w, d and v series and `fragment_arrays`, while a, b, c, x, y, z, the precursor and `fast_fragment` were unaffected. The engine's slices now carry the same exemption that a split has had since #113, because taking a peptide apart ion by ion divides a group between the pieces rather than losing it. The ions and their m/z are what 5.1.0 returned, to the last digit, for all thirteen ion types. Slicing an annotation across a group, and digesting or comparing coverage in a way that would cut one, still raise.
- `pt.averagine_comp()` and `pt.estimate_isotopic_distribution()` return a composition for a mass too small to show six isotope peaks, instead of raising `ValueError: zip() argument 2 is shorter than argument 1`. A candidate that small has fewer envelope peaks than the fractional reference it is compared against, and the comparison required equal lengths: `pt.averagine_comp(18.0106)` raised where 5.1.0 gave `{H: 2, O: 1}`, and 74 of the 128 masses on a quarter-dalton grid up to 32 Da were affected, none above. A peak the composition cannot produce now counts as the zero abundance it is, and a candidate carrying a peak the envelope does not have is rejected rather than compared. Compositions at every mass on that grid match 5.1.0, and masses above it are unchanged.
- `pt.fragmentation_preset(method, charge_state=...)` keeps the sign of the precursor charge. It took the magnitude, so `charge_state=-3` asked for charges 1 and 2 of a peptide carrying -3 and `pt.fragment("PEPTIDEK/-3", **pt.fragmentation_preset("cid", charge_state=-3))` returned the positive ions of a negative precursor, where the same call without the preset gives -2 and -1. `-3` now gives `charges=(-2, -1)` and `3` still gives `(1, 2)`: one charge per magnitude from 1 to `max(1, abs(charge_state) - 1)`, each with the sign of `charge_state`. The presets themselves are unchanged.
- `ProFormaAnnotation.to_ip2()` and `ProFormaAnnotation.to_diann()` raise `PeptacularError` instead of writing a terminal modification whose name holds a square bracket, such as `Formula:[13C2]H3`. Both readers find a terminal group with a bracket pattern that stops at the first `]`, so the written string either did not parse or parsed as something else: `pt.parse("EEN[Formula:[13C2]H3]-[UNIMOD:35]").to_ip2()` read back as `EEN[Formula:[13C2]H3][UNIMOD:35]`, moving the C-terminal modification onto the residue with no error, and `pt.parse("PEPTIDE-[Formula:[13C2]H3]").to_diann()` wrote a string `from_diann` rejects. `to_ip2` also refuses a C-terminal modification written after a last residue whose own name holds a bracket, which is the same ambiguity one position along. An internal modification name is read back unchanged and is still written, and so is every terminal name without a bracket.

### Changed

- `pt.averagine_comp()` caches its composition search per mass (`functools.lru_cache`, at most 1024 masses), so repeated calls with the same mass search once, and `pt.estimate_isotopic_distribution()`, which calls it on every call, no longer pays the search again. The cache holds an immutable tuple and every call returns a new `Counter`, so editing a returned composition cannot change what the next caller gets. Returned compositions are unchanged, including the 93.38% worst k=1..5 envelope error over the envelope test peptides. A mass that is new to the cache costs the same as before. The timings that measure the win are in the pull request (#107).
- Speed up `pt.coverage()`, `pt.percent_coverage()` and `find_indices()` on unmodified sequences by using `str.find` and direct slice assignment instead of regex matching and annotation slicing. The work it stops doing is one annotation slice per match: counting the calls on a 1600-residue protein with 444 tryptic peptides gives 3076 slices before this change and none after, for the same coverage vector. The coverage vector is unchanged for every combination of `accumulate`, `ignore_mods` and `ignore_ambiguity` on plain sequences, a modified protein, modified peptides, repeated and overlapping matches and ambiguous intervals, with the one exception in the next entry. The timings that measure the win are in the pull request (#86).
- `pt.coverage()`, `pt.percent_coverage()`, `pt.find_subsequence_indices()` and `pt.is_subsequence()` called with `ignore_mods=True` now return a result where they used to raise `PeptacularError`, when the protein holds an interval or a localization group that the match's slice would cut. The old path sliced the parent once per match even though the caller had asked for modifications to be ignored, and that slice refused the cut, so `pt.coverage("PE(PT)IDE", ["PEP"], ignore_mods=True)` raised instead of returning `[1, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0]`. With `ignore_mods=False` the slice still runs and still refuses, which is what keeps the refusal meaningful (#86).

### Added

- Add ProtParam property calculations `pt.instability_index()`, `pt.aliphatic_index()` and `pt.molar_extinction_coefficient()` across `property/core.py`, `AnnotationProperties` and `sequence/properties.py`, with support for single sequences, `ProFormaAnnotation` instances, and lists with parallel execution (#114).
- `pt.fragmentation_preset(method, charge_state=...)` returns the `pt.fragment()` keyword arguments for an activation method, so naming the method replaces writing the ion series, the neutral losses and the charge rule by hand: `pt.fragment(seq, **pt.fragmentation_preset("hcd", charge_state=2))`. Seven presets, each with the primary literature it rests on: `cid` and `hcd` (b, y), `etd` and `ecd` (c, z.), `ethcd` (b, y, c, z.), `ead` (a, b, c, x, y, z.) and `uvpd` (a, b, c, x, y, z), with water and ammonia losses (water only for `uvpd`) and at most one loss per ion. `charge_state=z` sets `charges=(1, ..., max(1, z - 1))`, the same rule in every preset. `etd` carries no b or y series, because the b and y ions of an electron-transfer experiment come from collisional activation of the charge-reduced survivor, which is what `ethcd` is for. The table is public and writable as `pt.FRAGMENTATION_PRESETS` and the citations are `pt.FRAGMENTATION_PRESET_CITATIONS`. Each method has one spelling, matched without regard to case or surrounding spaces, and an instrument's own name for a method (PASEF, ETciD) is mapped to a preset by whatever reads the file. A preset is a default and not a measurement: it names the series a method usually gives, and the real series depend on the instrument, the activation energy and the peptide, so the returned dict is a fresh copy and the caller's key wins when one is overridden. An unknown method raises `PeptacularError` naming the valid names. `fast_fragment()` takes three of the four keys, so filter the preset before splatting it there.
- `ProFormaAnnotation.to_maxquant()`, `ProFormaAnnotation.from_maxquant()` and `pt.convert_maxquant_sequence()` read and write MaxQuant modified sequences, the `Modified sequence` column of `evidence.txt` and `msms.txt`. The sequence is enclosed in underscores and each modification is written in round brackets after its residue, so `[ac]-SM[ox]K` becomes `_(ac)SM(ox)K_` and `PEP[Phospho]TIDE-[Amidated]` becomes `_PEP(Phospho)TIDE(Amidated)_`. The reader matches nested parentheses, so full names such as `_ALTDM(Oxidation (M))PQM(Oxidation (M))R_` read as `ALTDM[Oxidation (M)]PQM[Oxidation (M)]R`; a leading group is N-terminal, a group after the last residue is C-terminal and every other group sits on the residue before it. `to_maxquant()` copies modification strings through unchanged and raises `PeptacularError` for isotope labels, labile modifications, unknown-position modifications, intervals, charge or charge adducts, modification multipliers, more than one modification at a terminus or on one residue, a modification on the last residue (it would be read back as a C-terminal modification) and a modification name with unbalanced parentheses.
- `ProFormaAnnotation.to_diann()` writes an annotation as a DIA-NN sequence instead of raising `NotImplementedError`. The sequence is enclosed in underscores, internal modifications are written in square brackets after the residue they sit on, N-terminal modifications are written inside the leading underscore, and C-terminal modifications trail after the closing underscore, so `[Acetyl]-PEP[Phospho]TIDE-[Amidated]` becomes `_[Acetyl]PEP[Phospho]TIDE_[Amidated]`. Modification strings are copied through unchanged; reading the result with `from_diann` gives back an equal annotation. It raises `PeptacularError` for what DIA-NN cannot express: isotope labels, labile modifications, unknown-position modifications, intervals, charge and charge adducts, or modification multipliers. It also refuses two cases that `from_diann` would not read back at all, because the reader gives only the leading bracket group a dash and rewrites only a single trailing group: more than one N-terminal modification, which would be written as `_[Acetyl][Phospho]PEPTIDE_`, and more than one C-terminal modification, which would be written as `_PEPTIDE_[Amidated][Phospho]`. Both of those strings raise `ProFormaFormatError` when read.
- `ProFormaAnnotation.to_casanovo()` writes an annotation as a Casanovo sequence string instead of raising `NotImplementedError`. Casanovo writes modifications as signed delta masses with no brackets directly after the modified residue, and N-terminal modifications as signed delta masses at the very start of the string, so `[+42.011]-PEPM[+15.995]IDEC[+57.021]` becomes `+42.011PEPM+15.995IDEC+57.021`. The delta mass number is copied through unchanged; reading the result with `from_casanovo` gives back an equal annotation. It raises `PeptacularError` for what Casanovo cannot express: modifications that are not signed delta masses, multiple modifications on one residue, multiple N-terminal modifications, C-terminal modifications, isotope labels, labile modifications, unknown-position modifications, intervals, charge or charge adducts, or modification multipliers.
- `ProFormaAnnotation.to_ip2()` writes an annotation as an IP2 sequence instead of raising `NotImplementedError`. Each modification goes in parentheses directly after its residue, N-terminal modifications lead as parenthesis groups, and C-terminal modifications trail after the last residue's own modification, so `PEPTIDE[Phospho]-[Amidated]` becomes `PEPTIDE(Phospho)(Amidated)`. The modification string is copied unchanged and no flanking residues are written; reading the result with `from_ip2_sequence` gives back an equal annotation. It raises `PeptacularError` for what IP2 cannot place: isotope labels, labile modifications, unknown-position modifications, intervals, charge and charge adducts, and a C-terminal modification on a last residue with no modification of its own. It also refuses two cases that `from_ip2_sequence` would read back differently: more than one modification on the last residue, which the reader would split into residue and C-terminal modifications, and a modification name containing parentheses.

### Documentation

- `PROFORMA_COMPLIANCE.md` says which digest `diagnose(sequence, "digest")` checks. The operation runs `ProFormaAnnotation.digest_spans`, which locates the cut sites without building the peptides, so it reports success for a sequence whose peptides `pt.digest` refuses to build: `diagnose("PRT(ESFRMS)[+19.0523]ISK", "digest", enzyme="trypsin")` returns `None` while `pt.digest` on that sequence raises `PeptacularError: Interval [3:9] would be cut by slice [2:7]`. `docs/streaming.rst` already said the batch `digest` operation returns spans rather than `pt.digest` pairs, and the compliance file sent readers to `diagnose` without that caveat.
- Add a runnable localization example to the examples gallery.
- Add executable examples for all 17 amino-acid property scale functions.

_releases.body:
- Several improvements to the BLAT results page based on user feedback, including alignment mouseovers in hgTracks that show the query range and aligned bases
- Mismatch and insertion marks on alignment tracks are brighter and now have mouseovers that explain what they are
- Fixed bugs in the "Hide all other tracks" right-click option: hiding a track from the image now also updates its menu in the track list, and more buttons have icons
- New "My Data > Recent Browser Views" page that lists recently viewed browser states, behind an hg.conf setting that is off by default, and not yet on the RR
- Removed the broken Login link from the header of background status pages of hgSession and hgTables, such as the custom track backup page
- Faceted composite metadata with an apostrophe inside a word, as in "Peyer's patch", is no longer read as the start of a quoted field
- gff3ToGenePred now joins a multi-exon CDS that is a direct child of a gene, as in NCBI GFF files of EMBL-submitted assemblies
- BLAT result details pages once again show the alignment that was clicked, at the top of the list of the query's alignments
- When using the new BLAT page, pressing return to search again from the results page no longer loses the query sequence
- With quickLiftMultiChain off, a quickLifted item without blocks that two chains each partly covered was dropped as "Duplicated in new" (hg19 MRC1 lifted to hg38 vanished); such items now lift through the chain with the most aligned bases, for plain beds, ENCODE peaks, and GTEx genes, and on their details pages
- hgTrackUi prints filter labels and their tooltips more cleanly
- RepeatMasker Viz. in full mode at window sizes above 30 kb never drew an aligned block that started at the item's own start, so some repeats were missing entirely; these blocks are now drawn
- quickLift can now lift RepeatMasker tracks (rmsk, RepeatMasker Viz., and bigRmsk) in hgTracks and hgc, behind the browser.quickLiftRmsk setting, which is off by default and can be overridden by a cart variable
- Code review fixes for lifted RepeatMasker tracks: a lifted RepeatMasker Viz. track and the native one shared a layout, so one of them drew nothing, and the details page of a lifted rmsk item on a '-' chain showed the wrong Begin and Left in repeat; both now behave correctly
- hgc crashed when an rmskJoined track name was not in trackDb, and the bigRmsk details page did not check the bigBed column counts; hgc now handles both, skips missing .out and .align sections, and hgTracks builds the bigRmsk class table before tracks load in parallel
- quickLift kept lifted beds and peaks that landed outside the window, which produced the "map items spill over track bounds" warning; now only items that overlap the window are kept
- Reading many chains from a bigChain was quadratic (5,000 overlapping regions took 12 seconds per call); links are now grouped by chain id in one pass, which speeds up quickLift, bigChain tracks, hgc, and hgGene
- The list of vetted quickLift tracks was rebuilt on every call, and a composite view with no subtracks could crash quickLift; the list is now built once and an empty view is handled
- The hgc page for a lifted bed track showed the first item in the window, not the item that was clicked; it now shows the clicked item
- hgConvert stopped on a missing table when a composite's first view had no subtracks; each child of a composite is now checked on its own and empty views are skipped
- The faster bigChain link lookup now starts with a smaller hash, which removes a fixed cost on each call
- Final review fixes to lifted RepeatMasker details pages: duplicate rows, an error on a missing repeat, and a lifted bigRmsk item on the wrong chrom; each page now shows one correct item or a "not found" line
- hgTracks could corrupt memory when two bigRmsk tracks loaded at the same time with FreeType on; the FreeType width call used in the load threads is now locked
- A saved session with no db= in its contents crashed My Sessions, Backup Custom Tracks, and the Public Sessions gallery; all three now use one shared helper that handles a missing db and decodes the value
- Removed the svgBarChart hg.conf setting; SVG bar charts on the details page have been the default since v428
- Removed the useBlatBigPsl hg.conf setting; offering BLAT results as a bigPsl custom track has been the default since v349
- Removed the canSnake hg.conf setting; snake display for chain and alignment tracks has been the default since v468
- Removed the mergeRecommended hg.conf setting; merging a recommended track set into the current cart has been the default since v468
- Removed the canDupTracks hg.conf setting; duplicating a track has been the default since v444
- Removed the trackHubsCanAddGroups hg.conf setting; hub-defined track groups have been the default since v493
- hgLiftOver and hgConvert now offer liftOver to and from GenArk assemblies by default, without the genarkLiftOver hg.conf setting; a mirror with no genark table simply offers no GenArk assemblies
- BLAT results are now always saved as a custom track that can be reopened and shared, without the autoBlatBigPsl hg.conf setting
- Right-click "Zoom to this exon" (and enter codon/exon) in multi-region view gave an Error 500 or went to the wrong place; the menu now takes the chrom from the item's own link, and hgApi reports "Couldn't find item" instead of crashing
- hgApi exonToPos/codonToPos on a bigGenePred track labeled the answer with the requested chrom, so a multi-region caller got "multi:" with real coordinates; it now uses the chrom of the matching item
- For a bigGenePred name on two chroms (PAR copies, chrM/chrMT), hgApi exon zoom went to the wrong copy; it now prefers the match on the requested chrom
- A lifted RepeatMasker Viz. or bigRmsk item was dropped when none of its aligned blocks lifted, even when part of it lifted; it is now kept and drawn as a dashed unaligned extension, and its details page says that no aligned sequence maps
- The hgc details page of a quickLifted wig or bigWig now says when its values are in reverse order compared to the source assembly, and the message for a lifted wig with browser.quickLiftWig off uses the wording from QA
- Recommended track sets that connect a hub (ENIGMA, InSiGHT, and Exon Relevance) drew no hub tracks until the next page load; the hubs are now connected before the track list is built, so the tracks appear on the first load
- A lifted wig or bigWig with a logoMaf setting stopped hgTracks at base level with a database or maf error; lifted tracks now skip the source alignment and draw this assembly's base sized by the value
- A lifted rmsk or bigRmsk track left in a hub with browser.quickLiftRmsk off drew the source assembly's repeats at source coordinates; it now draws nothing, and with quickLiftMultiChain off an item in a segmental duplication is no longer dropped
- On hgc, a click on a bed 8, bed 9 without itemRgb, or bed 12 item lifted across species showed only the page title; the item is now lifted block by block as in hgTracks, and the page says so when no item matches
- Tidied the output of the RepeatMasker details pages
- The standard configuration page for composite tracks now lists a multiWig child of the composite, instead of the multiWig's own children, and links to the multiWig configuration page
- New trackDb setting heatmap.background sets the background color of heatmap displays; it should not be set to a color that could be confused with data values
- Fixed protein BLAT discarding alignments with overlapping query sequences
- A failing track inside a multiWig inside a composite now shows its error message instead of an empty yellow band
- A multiWig set to add or subtract no longer takes the page down when one of its children fails to load
- New track decorator setting decorator.default.maxDrawBases gives a window size in bases above which a decorator is not drawn, and warnings from tracks loaded in parallel, such as a decorator file that will not open, are now shown on the track instead of dropped
- Dot-bracket tracks no longer draw direction arrows in squish mode, where they read as structure
- The dotBracketColor setting now accepts colors written as #0000ff or blue, not only as 0,0,255, through a new colorSpec color-parsing library module
- New block of FreeType text rendering controls on the hgTracks configure page, for debugging font settings, behind the hg.conf setting freeTypeTuneUI
- Test fixes for barChartReorder, matrixNormalize, and mafToBigMafSummary, which left untracked files behind or failed under make -j
- gff3ToGenePred now includes pseudogenes in the resulting ncbiGene and ncbiRefSeq tracks
- Improved message packet handling between the parasol hub and node processes, which fixes long-running batches that made gigantic log files and stopped monitoring their long-running jobs
- New pushAccessions.sh script to push GenArk assemblies out to hgwbeta and the RR machines
- New pushContrib.sh script to push individual contrib tracks for a GenArk assembly
- New removal procedure for GenArk push maintenance to clean obsolete files from the /gbdb/genark/ hierarchy
- New compareLiftOverChains.py script to evaluate how well different alignment methods create liftOver files
- Reformatted the response email from the user liftOver request system
- Improved the automatic generation of common names for GenArk assemblies, to eliminate duplicated common names
- hgLogin no longer allows new usernames with leading or trailing spaces
- Fixed the chrom alias tooltip and the codon phase help icon in exon tooltips
- VCF REF allele strings are no longer copied onto the stack in hgvsGFromVariant() and vpGenomicToTranscript(), which long alleles could overflow
- A hub's directory row in Hub Space now leaves the db field blank and reads the genome from the hub's hub.txt file
- New Hub Space system measurement scripts, set up to run under the qateam account

_releases.body:
### Minor Changes

-   Upgrade from the `@janelia-flyem/neuroglancer@2.37.5` fork to mainline `neuroglancer@2.41.2`, with worker code (including WASM decoders) inlined as Blob-URL workers that are lazy-loaded when a Neuroglancer view mounts. (`@vitessce/neuroglancer`, `@vitessce/neuroglancer-workers`) ([#2693](https://github.com/vitessce/vitessce/pull/2693))

### Patch Changes

-   Fix linting issues with PR 2691. (`@vitessce/comparative`) ([#2699](https://github.com/vitessce/vitessce/pull/2699))

-   Support both single-cell and single-nucleus datasets in the comparative UI by changing the `datasetUrl` prop of `UncontrolledComparative` and `ControlledComparative` components to the explicit `singleCellDatasetUrl` and `singleNucleusDatasetUrl` props. Fix bugs with URL state management syncing. (`@vitessce/comparative`, `@vitessce/biomarker-select`, `@vitessce/styles`, `demo`) ([#2691](https://github.com/vitessce/vitessce/pull/2691))

-   Adjust vite and webpack configurations to account for latest Neuroglancer package version styling setup. Update the Neuroglancer styling overrides within Vitessce. (`@vitessce/neuroglancer`) ([#2693](https://github.com/vitessce/vitessce/pull/2693))

-   Fix on-demand mesh loading in the docs build, where Docusaurus’s Babel transform broke Set spread ([...set] -> [set]). (`@vitessce/example-configs`, `docs`) ([#2689](https://github.com/vitessce/vitessce/pull/2689))
### Versioned Sites
- [Docs](https://legacy.vitessce.io/docs/2026-11-17/ed270388/)
